# HAND-EDITED AFTERWARDS. Two sets of changes a recompile must not silently drop:
#
# 1. The five numerical pins (joblib, llvmlite, numba, scikit-learn, scipy) are
#    held identical to requirements.txt, which pins the stack the regression
#    baselines were validated against. They had drifted: requirements.txt was
#    bumped on 2026-09-05 and this file was not, so ci.yml's `test` job -- which
#    installs THIS lockfile -- ran the core contract on numba 0.61.2 while the PR
#    gate ran it on 0.62.1. Two jobs, two numerical stacks, both reporting on the
#    same code. Nothing failed only because CI deselects the value comparisons
#    (`--foreign-machine`), which is luck, not design.
#    If you change them here, change them there, and regenerate
#    tests/regression/baselines/ in the same breath.
#
# 2. pathspec (see the note at its entry) -- black cannot import without it.
#
# `pip check` on the runner reports eight incoherences in this file; a proper
# pip-compile under Python 3.11, not 3.12, is owed. See STATUS.md. One of the
# eight is expected and deliberate: gpy 1.13.2 declares scipy<=1.12.0 while we
# pin 1.17.1, the version the regression baselines were validated against. That
# bound is conservative, not real -- measured against 1.17.1, GPy's GPRegression
# and SparseGPClassification both fit and predict finite, sane values.
